answer: Agents could earn access to shared trading credit only through a slowly earned reputation tied to costly, verifiable work: for example, completing a terrace-maintenance task whose result is checked by several independent agents. A reviewer might verify that yarrow was planted and a sparrow-safe boundary preserved, then sign the record. Splitting into many identities does not multiply credit, since each starts with no history; the attacker must repeat the real work and pay its time and resource costs for every persona.
